FRT.name: Federal Realty Investment Trust
kill_criteria: Comparable Property Operating Income (same-property NOI proxy) growth below 2% for two consecutive quarters (below the recent 2.8-4.9% band)
Net debt/EBITDAre above ~6.5x (from ~5.3x at 2026-06-30), or any senior-notes covenant cushion closing to within 25% of its minimum/maximum
A cut (not merely a tighten) to FFO or Core FFO guidance versus the immediately preceding quarter's range
Occupancy or leased rate down more than 100bp year-over-year for two consecutive quarters
The 59-consecutive-year dividend-increase streak broken, or payout ratio above ~90% of Core FFO
key_adverse_facts: Net debt rose 8.1% in two quarters (Dec 2025 $4,310.5M to Jun 2026 $4,660.7M net debt); net debt/EBITDAre approx 5.3x
$400M of 1.25%-coupon senior notes matured Feb 2026 and were refinanced into materially higher-cost term-loan/revolver debt - a real interest-expense headwind

Headline GAAP EPS growth in 2025-2026 was substantially driven by gains on sale of real estate and a one-off $13.0M/$0.15-per-share New Markets Tax Credit item in Q2 2025 (excluded by management from Core FFO), not organic FFO growth
FRT introduced a new non-GAAP metric ('Core FFO') at Q4 2025, a definitional break versus the prior Nareit-FFO-only track record
An 8-K filed 2026-08-11 (items 1.01/2.03/3.02/8.01/9.01, likely financing-related) postdates this dossier's research window and was not reviewed

LMT.name: Lockheed Martin Corporation
kill_criteria: Any newly disclosed reach-forward or classified-program charge exceeding approximately $300M pretax in a single quarter
Aeronautics segment backlog falling below the 2026-06-30 level of $54.4B at the next 10-Q (a third consecutive quarterly decline)
Full-year 2026 F-35 deliveries pacing materially below the ~150-155 unit annual run-rate implied by FY2025's 191 units (e.g. under ~100-110 units through Q3 2026)
A guidance cut (not reaffirmation) to FY2026 sales, segment operating profit, or free cash flow at either of the next two earnings releases
A continuing resolution or government shutdown lasting beyond one quarter that management explicitly attributes a revenue or cash-flow shortfall to
key_adverse_facts: FY2024: $2.0 billion pretax ($1.5B / $6.16-per-share after-tax) of classified-program losses across Aeronautics ($555M cumulative) and Missiles and Fire Control ($1.4B cumulative, where the company now deems it probable that all remaining fixed-price contract options on one classified program will be exercised at a loss)

Q2 2025: an additional $950M reach-forward loss on the SAME classified Aeronautics program (issues 'continued into 2025' with greater impact than previously estimated - i.e. not resolved by the FY2024 charge), plus $570M and $95M losses on two Sikorsky/RMS international helicopter programs (CMHP, TUHP), plus a $66M NGAD-related asset write-off and a $103M tax charge - $1.6B + $169M total, ~$5.83 per share combined impact; cash from operations fell to $201M and free cash flow went negative $(150)M that quarter
Q4 2025: a further $479M ($1.63 per share after-tax) non-operational pension-settlement charge

Q1 2026: additional smaller unfavorable adjustments on F-16 ($125M, production performance/development delays) and C-130 ($55M, diminishing manufacturing sources); C-130J annual deliveries collapsed from 21 units (FY2024) to 2 units (FY2025); cash from operations fell to $220M and free cash flow was negative $(291)M

In total, the charge pattern spans two consecutive fiscal years and at least four distinct programs/business units (Aeronautics classified x2, MFC classified, RMS/Sikorsky x2), plus newly disclosed F-16/C-130J issues - a recurring pattern of program-execution and cost-estimation risk, not an isolated event, and by definition classified-program specifics cannot be independently verified from public filings

F-35 deliveries decelerated sharply in H1 2026 (51 units vs 97 units in H1 2025, -47% YoY) at the same time Aeronautics segment backlog has declined for two consecutive periods (Dec 2024 $62.8B to Dec 2025 $59.4B to Jun 2026 $54.4B)

The 8-K filed 2026-08-28 is a new $2.25bn 364-day revolving credit agreement (resolved by DVH4 2026-10-06); full FY2025 10-K critical-audit-matters/related-party/Form 4 review and independent recomputation of whether FY2025 cash-flow guidance was met were not completed this pass (FY25 FCF was $6,908M against guidance of ~$6,600M). No share repurchases were made in H1 2026, and the $3.45bn Ultra Maritime acquisition (signed 6 Jul 2026, expected to close Q4 2026) will be funded with cash and new financing. [Corrected 2026-10-06, DVH4]
